units: <cite ref="Gittin 44b:7">Git. 44ᵇ</cite> <he>אית ליה א׳ וכ׳</he> he has a lodging place in Palestine, (is an occasional resident), opp. <cite ref="B00756"><he>ביתא</he></cite> permanent home.

<cite ref="Megillah 26a">Meg. 26ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Yoma 12a">Yoma 12ᵃ</cite> it is customary to leave empty jars and hides of slaughtered animals (<cite ref="L00000"><he>ל</he></cite>) <he>באושפיזֵיה</he> in one’s inn.

<cite ref="Zevachim 61b:7">Zeb. 61ᵇ</cite> <he>א׳ הוה נקט וכ׳</he> (Ms. M. <he>אוּשְׁפְּזִיכָא … נקיטא</he>, v. <cite ref="A00934"><he>אושפיזכן</he></cite>; v. Rabb. D. S. a. l.) the Divine fire took up its abode now here and now there.

<cite ref="Eruvin 53b:12">Erub. 53ᵇ</cite> <he>שאיל בא׳</he> (Rashi <he>משייל בעניין אושפזיכני</he>, read <he>ניה …</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note 80) inquired after the character of an inn (of his landlord).

<cite ref="Eruvin 53b:12">Ib.</cite> (enigmatic inquiry that the landlord might not overhear it) <he>גבר פום דין חי מה טיבו</he> Ar. (v. Rabb. l. c. note 90) = <he>איש־פי־ז־נא</he> our inn—what is its character?
